clips.title: Chase Hughes: How to Get Info Without Asking
clips.desc: Behavior expert Chase Hughes on elicitation: make a wrong statement and people correct you (Whole Foods pay, Uber drivers), use statements instead of questions, then disbelief.
clips.transcript: I'll give you an example. Let's say you and I walk into Whole Foods. Let's say there's a young lady stocking produce and you get in there and I say, your goal is to go figure out how much she makes in 60 seconds and you're not allowed to ask any questions. So if you went over to her and this is a generalization just to get you to understand what elicitation is and said, hey, I'm trying to find the baby carrots and she walks you over there, but while you're walking you say, I just read this article online that says all Whole Foods employees just got bumped up to $26 an hour. That's fantastic. And she turns around and goes, what? No, I make 17. So now she doesn't feel like she's been pressed or questioned about how much she makes. She's correcting you. Or let's say you got into an Uber tonight and you said, I just read this article that Uber drivers were one of the top, most highly satisfied employees in the country. You're gonna get a correction and you're gonna be like, where did you read that? So triggering a need to correct the record is one of the easiest ways to use elicitation but it's only one. Another one is just making a statement afterwards and saying, I bet you had some interesting experiences doing that or I can imagine that was challenging. Statements are always gonna be better than asking pointed questions because a person feels like they're volunteering information. The third layer of that is disbelief. So let's say I wanted to ask if you just got back from vacation and I didn't wanna use any questions. We, let's say we meet up for dinner or something and I said, see, you look like you just got back from a vacation. That's the statement. And you're like, no, actually I've been doing this, this, this, and this. So now you've given me more than if I had just asked if you were on vacation. And I said, wow, that had to be interesting. I can't imagine that there's gotta be a lot of stuff going on there. And you start talking more and more and more. And then
clips.doc_desc: How to get info out of people

clips.title: Buda Unveils a Giant Wiener Dog Statue
clips.desc: KVUE news report: a 19-foot-long, 10-foot-tall wiener dog sculpture in Buda City Park, a tribute to the Wiener Dog Races' 30th anniversary.
clips.transcript: The Buda Economic Development Corporation is honoring a well -known tradition in its town. Earlier today, they unveiled a 19 -foot -long, 10 -foot -tall wiener dog sculpture in Buda City Park. Now, it's a tribute to their annual wiener dog races, which will celebrate its 30th anniversary this April. The EDC says it can also become a roadside attraction, inviting travelers to grab a picture and support local businesses.

clips.title: Drew Lynch: Europe Refuses to Update Their Roads
clips.desc: Comic Drew Lynch hauling a suitcase up cobblestone hills: no asphalt, hotels with no elevator, cars honking at you on the sidewalk.
clips.transcript: can someone please explain to me why Europe refuses to update their roads everywhere else in the world has discovered asphalt and Europe is like yeah we put your hotel at the top of a cobblestone hill where you have to haul your suitcase on a street that's somehow not made for wheels and the entire time you're swimming upstream against families who are laughing and pointing at buildings smiling eating gelato having a way different day than you because your back hasn't stopped sweating since the plane landed and cars are honking at you on the sidewalk and you're like wait am I in the street or is a car on the sidewalk right now how is a car on the sidewalk and your hands are filled with luggage so you can't check your pants to see if you've been pickpocketed yet but you kind of hope somebody would take your pants because it's so hot outside you wore pants because the planes are cold but then when you land it's scorching outside but inside it's somehow hotter than outside because Europe also hasn't discovered air conditioning yet and you keep asking your partner it's up ahead hey are we almost there yet that they can't hear you over the clacking of your luggage's suitcase being assaulted by the ground because the floor is made of brick that's been around since before Christ you finally get to your hotel and you're wet and exhausted they tell you your rooms at the top of the set of stairs where each step is somehow narrower than a drink menu and you can't use an elevator because this hotel is actually just some old lady's house because your partner booked through a third party to save $40 so you haul this fat American sweaty suitcase up through a doorframe that's at the top of the stairs and the room is the width of a yoga mat because that's Europe baby but hey they make the bread fresh here
clips.doc_desc: Drew Lynch walking down Euro cobblestones with his take on traveling to Europe
